analysis:
Both units are base_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (base lines 458-880: unreleased v0.10.7-era entries and the v0.10.6 release notes). The PR patch is documentation only: it replaces the v0.10.8 candidate heading with v0.10.9 and adds roughly 390 lines of release notes at head lines 11-400. The supplied patch excerpt is truncated, so most of the new head text was not visible to me. I saw no code, configuration, key handling, authorization, attestation, or encryption changes in the supplied evidence.

The base text I reviewed only records previously described behavior, such as cluster pair approvals, the SSD prefix cache, the enabled-model filter, and sandbox setup. It touches threat areas T-041 (prefix cache), TB-012/TB-013 (add-on and sandbox installer) and TB-014 (GPU limit), but only as changelog prose. It introduces no new attack surface and I found no invalidated assumption or security regression. Changelog statements, for example that rolled-back releases are quarantined, are claims that cannot be checked here without the corresponding source diffs.

Remaining question for integration: the head side of CHANGELOG.md (new v0.10.9 notes) was only partially visible. If other batches show source changes in the pair update, rollback, prefix-cache, or installer paths, the changelog claims should be checked against those code changes. No finding is warranted from these units alone.
